s1.syndrome_frame: Recurring skin eruptions with vesicles and bullae in a child, starting at birth
salient_findings: Hyperkeratotic plaques with distinct borders and annular appearance
key_facts: Normal growth and development for age and sex
Multiple areas of erythema, vesicles, and bullae on face, trunk, and extremities
Skin-punch biopsy revealed hyperkeratosis and bullae formation
Genetic testing revealed a heterozygous variation c.482T>C (p. L161P) in KRT1

raw.syndrome_frame: Recurring skin eruptions with vesicles and bullae in a child, starting at birth
salient_findings: Hyperkeratotic plaques with distinct borders and annular appearance
key_facts: Normal growth and development for age and sex
Multiple areas of erythema, vesicles, and bullae on face, trunk, and extremities
Skin-punch biopsy revealed hyperkeratosis and bullae formation
Genetic testing revealed a heterozygous variation c.482T>C (p. L161P) in KRT1

raw.rationale: The presence of hyperkeratotic plaques, distinct vacuolization in the granular and upper spinous layers, and bullae formation within the epidermis, along with the genetic variation c.482T>C (p. L161P) in KRT1, are consistent with psoriasis, particularly the histopathological findings and the development of thickened, brown, corrugated plaques over time.

rejected.label: bullous pemphigoid
rejected.why: Unremarkable direct immunofluorescence results do not support this diagnosis

rejected.label: dermatitis
rejected.why: Lack of specific findings such as spongiosis and eosinophilic infiltration

rejected.label: eczema
rejected.why: Clinical presentation and histopathology do not align with typical eczema features

rejected.label: eruption
rejected.why: Too nonspecific and does not account for the specific histopathological and genetic findings
